Cite the Camera Trap Data Packages Used in an Analysis

Source: R/cite_datapackages.R
cite_datapackages.Rd

Builds a reference for each data package in a list, ready to paste into a manuscript, import into a reference manager, or keep as a table. Works on any Camtrap DP package, from WildObs or elsewhere:

  • When a package carries a bibliographicCitation, that text is the reference, word for word, because it is the one the data providers asked for. WildObs citations end with the project's RAiD.

  • Otherwise the reference is built from the Camtrap DP descriptor: authors from contributors (people with the role contact, principalInvestigator or contributor, or no role; never rightsHolder, publisher or funder), the year created, title, and homepage, else id.

With include_version = TRUE the version of the data is appended: for WildObs packages the data package version (versionControlWildObs), which is specific to each project and rises whenever WildObs corrects its data; otherwise the package version, unless it is only the Camtrap DP standard version named in profile or the citation already gives it.

With covariates = TRUE, the products behind the WildObs covariates (e.g. the Forest Landscape Integrity Index or the human footprint) are cited too, once each. They are read from the custom$source$citation of each field in the covariates table schema, so only packages downloaded with their tables have them.

Usage

cite_datapackages(
  dp_list,
  format = c("text", "bibtex", "data.frame"),
  sort_by = c("author", "year", "none"),
  include_version = TRUE,
  accessed = NULL,
  covariates = FALSE
)

Arguments

dp_list

A list of data packages, such as the result of wildobs_dp_download(), or a single data package. Packages downloaded with metadata_only = TRUE can be cited too.

format

The form of the result: "text" (default) for one formatted reference per package, "bibtex" for a utils::bibentry() object that utils::toBibtex() writes as BibTeX, or "data.frame" for one row per reference.

sort_by

How to order the references: "author" (default, alphabetically by the first author's family name, as most reference lists are), "year" (oldest first, then by author), or "none" (the order of dp_list).

include_version

Logical. Append the version of the data to each reference? Defaults to TRUE, because a project's data can be corrected between downloads.

accessed

Optional date the data were downloaded, as a Date or a "YYYY-MM-DD" string, appended as "Accessed YYYY-MM-DD.". Defaults to NULL (left out).

covariates

Logical. Also cite the products behind the covariates table? Defaults to FALSE.

Value

Depends on format:

"text"

A character vector of references, named by package id. The covariate product citations, if asked for, follow, each named by the covariates it is behind, without their spatial scale (e.g. "FLII", or "mean_monthly_precipitation; mean_monthly_temperature" for a product behind several).

"bibtex"

A utils::bibentry() object: one @misc entry per package, keyed by package id, plus one per covariate product, keyed by its first covariate.

"data.frame"

One row per reference, with columns type ("data package" or "covariate product"), id, authors, year, title, version, identifier (RAiD or DOI where there is one), url (the identifier, else the package homepage or id), licenses and citation.

Stops if dp_list holds something that is not a data package, or if a package has neither a bibliographicCitation nor a title to build one from.

See also

wildobs_dp_download() to download the packages; extract_metadata() for their contributors, licences and related identifiers as tables.

Author

Zachary Amir

Examples

# any Camtrap DP package can be cited, here the camtrapdp package's example
if (requireNamespace("camtrapdp", quietly = TRUE)) {
  x <- camtrapdp::example_dataset()
  cite_datapackages(x)
  # as a table, with the date the data were accessed
  cite_datapackages(x, format = "data.frame", accessed = "2026-10-15")
  # or as BibTeX for a reference manager
  utils::toBibtex(cite_datapackages(x, format = "bibtex"))
}
#> @Misc{7cca70f5-ef8c-4f86-85fb-8f070937d7ab,
#>   title = {Sample from: MICA - Muskrat and coypu camera trap observations in Belgium, the Netherlands and Germany},
#>   author = {P Desmet and A Neukermans and D {Van der beeck} and E Cartuyvels},
#>   year = {2022},
#>   note = {Licence: CC0-1.0; http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/},
#>   url = {https://camtrap-dp.tdwg.org/example/},
#> }

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# cite every WildObs project downloaded for an analysis, and the covariate products
api_key <- Sys.getenv("WILDOBSR_API_KEY")
wet_tropics <- list(xmin = 144.9, xmax = 146.5, ymin = -19.6, ymax = -15.3)
ids <- wildobs_mongo_query(api_key = api_key, spatial = wet_tropics,
                           tabularSharingPreference = "open")
dp_list <- wildobs_dp_download(api_key = api_key, project_ids = ids)
writeLines(cite_datapackages(dp_list, covariates = TRUE, accessed = Sys.Date()))
} # }
